OPEN.name: OPEN
OPEN.desc: For athletes new to HYROX with basic strength/weightlifting knowledge. 10K time: <1 hour.

days.workout:
BENCHMARK · TEST DAY
Warm up well first, then record every score.

1) 1km run — time trial
2) rest 5 min
3) 500m ski OR row — time trial
   (pick the machine you'll retest on)
4) rest 5 min
5) Max unbroken Wall balls (9/6kg)
6) rest 3 min
7) Max Push ups in 2 min
days.notes: This is your baseline — the numbers we measure progress against, so log all of them. Give each test a real, honest effort, but you're an athlete checking fitness, not chasing a one-off hero score. Warm up properly first: 5-10 min easy cardio plus some dynamic drills. Always retest on the same ski/row machine so the comparison is fair. There's no perfect score here — this is simply your starting point. We'll repeat this in a later block to see how far you've come.

days.notes:

R1: 600m + 20 each
R2: 400m + 15 each

DB snatch: one clean pull from floor to overhead, alternate hands. Goblet squat: elbows inside the knees, full depth. Sled push: low hips, long steady steps — lighten the load if you can't keep moving.

Shoulder press: ribs down, don't arch the low back. This is accessory strength — keep rest generous and form crisp.

BENCHMARK · TEST DAY

1) 12-min run/walk — max distance

4) Max Air squats in 90 sec
5) Plank hold — max time

Finish: 5-10 min easy walk
days.notes: This is your starting line — write the numbers down so you can see how far you come. The 12-min run/walk: cover as much ground as you can while staying in control; walking is completely fine. Push ups and squats: stop a rep or two before total failure and keep good form (knee push ups absolutely count). Plank: hold a straight line and drop the moment your hips start to sag. Warm up easy for 5 min first. No perfect score exists — this is just where you begin today, and we'll retest later to prove your progress.

Each block slightly quicker than the last

sledpull.name: Sled Pull
sledpull.blurb: Dial in your pull technique and build the back and grip to keep it moving.

workouts.title: Technique Sets
workouts.workout:
5 sets
12.5m sled pull — alternate styles
(arms-only / walk-back)
rest 75 sec
workouts.notes: Practice both methods to find which is faster for you. Brace the core, pull hand-over-hand, and keep the rope low and tight.

workouts.title: Pull + Grip Combo
workouts.workout:
4 rounds
12.5m sled pull (arms only)
40m farmer carry (heavy)
rest 90 sec
workouts.notes: Stacks two grip-heavy stations so your forearms learn to keep working. Relax the hands between efforts — don't death-grip from the start.

workouts.title: Heavy Pull Capacity
workouts.workout:
6 × 12.5m sled pull (heavy)
60 sec rest
workouts.notes: Builds the raw back and grip strength to move a loaded sled. As heavy as possible, but you must complete each length unbroken.

farmers.name: Farmers Carry
farmers.blurb: Bullet-proof your grip and learn to carry tall and fast under heavy load.

workouts.title: Carry Intervals
workouts.workout:
5 × 100m farmer carry (heavy)
90 sec rest
workouts.notes: Tall posture, shoulders packed, core braced. Heavy enough to challenge the grip but light enough to stay unbroken across each 100m.

workouts.title: Grip Under Fatigue
workouts.workout:
4 rounds
80m farmer carry
15 KB deadlift
8 cal ski
60 sec rest
workouts.notes: Pre-fatigues the grip so carrying late in a race feels easier. Chalk up, and relax the hands the moment you set the weight down.

workouts.title: Long Carry + Run
workouts.workout:
3 rounds
150m farmer carry
400m run
2 min rest
workouts.notes: Teaches you to run with a wrecked grip and recover it on the move. Break the carry once if needed rather than letting the run pace collapse.

lunge.name: Sandbag Lunge
lunge.blurb: Develop the leg endurance and bracing to lunge cleanly on dead legs.

workouts.title: Lunge Volume
workouts.workout:
4 sets
20 Sandbag lunge (20/10kg)
rest 75 sec
workouts.notes: Sandbag high on the shoulders, torso tall, back knee kisses the floor. Keep it unbroken; scale the load before you ever shorten the range.

workouts.title: Lunge + Run
workouts.workout:
4 rounds
25m sandbag lunge
300m run
90 sec rest
workouts.notes: Builds quads that keep lunging after running has pre-fatigued the legs. Even, deliberate steps — don't rush and lose depth or balance.

workouts.title: Descending Burner
workouts.workout:
For time
40-30-20-10
• Sandbag lunge (20/10kg)
• Air squat
workouts.notes: High-volume leg endurance to harden your lunge. Plan your breaks early so the round of 40 doesn't blow you up for the rest of the workout.

ski.name: SkiErg
ski.blurb: Sharpen your ski technique and the pacing to open and close strong.

workouts.title: Ski Intervals
workouts.workout:
6 × 250m ski
90 sec rest
record every split
workouts.notes: Drive from the hips and lats, not just the arms — it's a full-body pull. Hold an even split across all six; consistency beats one fast rep.

workouts.title: Pacing Pyramid
workouts.workout:
100-200-300-200-100m ski
rest = seconds of the piece just done
workouts.notes: Learn to pace by feel as the distance changes each set. Keep the stroke rate controlled and the pull long and smooth.

workouts.title: Ski to Run
workouts.workout:
5 rounds
200m ski
200m run
60 sec rest
workouts.notes: Practice opening the legs up after the upper-body burn of the ski. Settle your breathing over the first 50m of the run, then build.

row.name: Row
row.blurb: Build a powerful, repeatable stroke and the discipline to pace it.

workouts.title: Row Intervals
workouts.workout:
6 × 250m row
90 sec rest
record every split
workouts.notes: Legs-core-arms on the drive, arms-core-legs on the recovery. Hold an even, repeatable split across all six efforts.

workouts.title: Negative Split 1k
workouts.workout:
1000m row
negative split every 250m
(each quarter quicker than the last)
workouts.notes: Start controlled and build so the final 250m is fastest. Trains the pacing discipline that stops you blowing up early on race day.

workouts.title: Row + Burpee Buffer
workouts.workout:
E2MOM × 8
200m row
5 burpees
rest the remainder
workouts.notes: Keeps the engine working through interruptions, like a real race. Step over on the burpees to save your legs if you're fading.

burpee.name: Burpee Broad Jump
burpee.blurb: Make the most draining station efficient with better mechanics and pacing.

workouts.title: Efficiency Sets
workouts.workout:
5 sets
10m burpee broad jump
rest 60 sec
focus: fewest, longest jumps
workouts.notes: Plant hands close to feet, explode the hips, land soft and balanced. Fewer, longer jumps mean less time and far less wasted energy.

workouts.title: BBJ Pacing
workouts.workout:
4 rounds
15m burpee broad jump
200m run
90 sec rest
workouts.notes: Find a sustainable BBJ rhythm you can repeat after running. Steady breathing — this station spikes the heart rate faster than any other.

workouts.title: BBJ + Core
workouts.workout:
3 rounds
12 burpee broad jump
20 sit-ups
10 cal any machine
60 sec rest
workouts.notes: Builds the hip power and trunk endurance the broad jump demands. Keep the chest-to-floor standard honest even when you're tired.

run.name: Compromised Running
run.blurb: The race is won between stations. Train running on legs that already hurt.

workouts.title: Run Off Sled
workouts.workout:
E2MOM × 10
10m sled push
200m run
rest the remainder
workouts.notes: The single most race-specific drill — running on dead legs. Quick turnover and stay tall; the pace will feel slow, and that's completely normal.

workouts.title: Station to Run
workouts.workout:
5 rounds
20 Wall balls (9/6kg)
400m run
90 sec rest
workouts.notes: Trains the jump from a leg-burning station into a steady run. Don't sprint out of the station — settle into rhythm first, then build.

workouts.title: Negative-Split Run
workouts.workout:
Run 30 min
lift the pace every 6 min
(final block the fastest)
workouts.notes: Pace control under fatigue is what wins HYROX. Start almost too easy so the final block is the hardest part — never the first.

grip.name: Grip
grip.blurb: A failing grip wrecks the carry, the pull and the wall balls. Fix the root.

workouts.title: Grip Stack
workouts.workout:
4 rounds
40m farmer carry (heavy)
12.5m sled pull
8 KB deadlift
rest 90 sec
workouts.notes: Three grip-heavy movements back to back to build forearm stamina. Relax the hands whenever you set down — grip recovers fast if you let it.

workouts.title: Dead Hang + Carry
workouts.workout:
5 sets
max dead hang
→ 60m farmer carry
rest 90 sec
workouts.notes: The hang builds raw grip; the carry trains it under load and movement. Stop the hang 2-3 sec before failure to keep every set high quality.

workouts.title: Long Carry Endurance
workouts.workout:
3 × 200m farmer carry
2 min rest
break as few times as possible
workouts.notes: Pure grip endurance for the longest carries. Choose a weight you can hold for at least 100m unbroken before the first break.

engine.name: Engine
engine.blurb: Raise your sustainable output so every station and run feels easier.

workouts.title: Lactate EMOM
workouts.workout:
16 min EMOM
min 1: 15 cal row
min 2: 15 Wall balls
min 3: 12 burpees
min 4: rest
workouts.notes: Hard but repeatable — aim for the same output every round. Find the pace you can hold to the last set without falling off a cliff.

workouts.title: Threshold Machine
workouts.workout:
5 × 3 min hard / 90 sec easy
(ski, row or bike)
record each effort
workouts.notes: Builds the high-end engine you can actually hold. 'Hard' means comfortably uncomfortable and repeatable for all five — not an all-out sprint.

workouts.title: Mixed Chipper
workouts.workout:
For time
1000m row
800m run
50 Wall balls
40 cal ski
30 burpees
workouts.notes: A long, steady grind to raise your aerobic ceiling. Pick one pace you can hold throughout rather than going out hot and blowing up.
